title: Coprime congruence images force equality of the integral representation kernels
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_E$, extending absolute value $|\cdot|_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\pi=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $H$ be any group, let $r\geq0$ be an integer, and let $A:H\to\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathcal O)$ be a group homomorphism. Here matrices are as in [def-weil-matrix], and $\operatorname{GL}_r(R)$ is the group of matrices admitting a two-sided matrix inverse. For $n\geq1$, let $A_n:H\to\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathcal O/\pi^n\mathcal O)$ be entrywise reduction, let $Q_n=A_n(H)$, and let $K_n=\{h\in H:A_n(h)=I_r\}$. Assume that for every $n\geq1$ the group $Q_n$ is finite and $\gcd(|Q_n|,\ell)=1$. Then $K_1=K_n=\ker A$ for every $n\geq1$, where $\ker A=\{h\in H:A(h)=I_r\}$. No topology or continuity is assumed on $H$ or $A$, and the rank-zero case is included.

source.place: Agent algebraic corollary to Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3 (not stated in the notes): first-order matrix power congruence, induction on congruence depth, and norm separatedness (old item Steps 3-5).

proof.text: Put I = span {π}, with the recorded coefficient uniformizer π. Extract the local-ring and DVR structures, maximal ideal m, its absolute-value membership criterion, and I = m from lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr. Hence I is proper and the integer ring is Noetherian. Spectral norm extension and Padic.norm_p_lt_one show |ℓ|_E < 1, so ℓ belongs to m = I. No topology on H is needed.

source.place: Agent algebraic supplement to Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3: coefficient normalization, not a theorem asserted in those notes.

proof.text: For n ≥ 1 and h in K_n, quotient equality says every entry of B = A(h) - I_r lies in I^n. Reduce B modulo I^(n+1) to get X. Each summand of each entry of X*X is zero: the corresponding product belongs to I^(n+n), contained in I^(n+1). Also ℓX = 0 because ℓ belongs to I. Induction using distributivity and X*X = 0 gives (1+X)^m = 1 + m • X. Thus A_(n+1)(h)^ℓ = 1. The proof is a generic private congruence_power lemma for any ideal of a commutative ring and any exponent p belonging to that ideal.

source.place: Agent algebraic supplement to Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3: first-order power congruence (square-zero calculation).

proof.text: Induct on $n\geq1$ to prove $K_1=K_n$. At $n=1$ this is reflexive. Suppose $K_1=K_n$ and let $h\in K_1$. Then $h\in K_n$, and Step 2 gives $x^\ell=I_r$ for $x=A_{n+1}(h)\in Q_{n+1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-matrix-group-coprime-power] to the subgroup $Q_{n+1}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathcal O/\pi^{n+1}\mathcal O)$ and exponent $\ell$. Its finiteness and $\gcd(|Q_{n+1}|,\ell)=1$ are exactly the assumptions of the item. Injectivity of its power map, together with $I_r^\ell=I_r$, gives $x=I_r$ and $h\in K_{n+1}$. Conversely, $K_{n+1}\subseteq K_1$ follows entrywise from $\pi^{n+1}\mathcal O\subseteq\pi\mathcal O$. This completes the induction.

source.place: Agent algebraic supplement to Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3: kernel induction; power-map input is Mathlib/GroupTheory/OrderOfElement.lean:1245-1247.

proof.text: For h in K_1, Step 3 places every entry of A(h)-I_r in I^n for every n ≥ 1; level zero is automatic because I^0 is the unit ideal. The recorded integer ring is a DVR, hence Noetherian, and local by lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr. Since I is its proper maximal ideal, apply Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing (RingTheory/Filtration.lean) to show the intersection of all its powers is zero. Every matrix entry of A(h)-I_r is therefore zero, giving A(h)=I_r. This replaces the longer unit-times-uniformizer factorization/norm estimate with Krull intersection.

source.place: Agent algebraic supplement to Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3: separatedness by the existing DVR factorization and unit-norm clauses.

proof.text: Step 4 gives $K_1\subseteq\ker A$. The reverse inclusion follows by reducing the identity matrix modulo $\pi$. Thus $K_1=\ker A$, and Step 3 gives $K_n=K_1=\ker A$ for every $n\geq1$. If $r=0$, the unique empty matrix is the identity and every group $\operatorname{GL}_0$ is trivial: all these kernels are $H$. The entrywise arguments above are also vacuous in that case.
